newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline ends lower but bucks seasonal trend.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline ends lower but bucks seasonal trend.

text.p: NWE gasoline prices ended slightly lower on Monday after an early drop in crude oil, but some traders said gasoline was on solid footing after material was sent to the States and refiners here focused on gas oil production.

The arbitrage from both NWE and the Med to the U.S. was close to or already shut, traders said, but some sellers may still choose to send material across the Atlantic for certain sizes and delivery periods.
"I think it's relatively strong for this time of year," said one London trader. "Definitely there is more stuff going to the U.S."
Eurograde barges ended $2 lower at $216 fob ARA, where it was last heard traded for 500 tonnes of prompt material. Earlier, $217 traded for first-half February delivery.
Regular unleaded stayed about $8 lower at $207/$209 fob ARA in very quiet dealings.
In the cargo market, high freight rates and lack of material continued to limit trading.
"Relatively speaking mogas is strong but it all depends on what the crude market is doing," one trader at a major said.
In the Med, steady demand from Lebanon and other eastern Mediterranean destinations for Italian material continued to support prices, a trader said.
"The eastern Med demand is there...The Med market fundamentally is balanced," she said.
About one million to 1.5 million tonnes likely moved from the Med to the U.S. in January, about the normal level, and a similar amount could move in the first half of February, she said.
IPE March Brent futures traded lower for most of the session before holding support at $22 a barrel and bouncing up to $22.32 by 1742 GMT, up six cents.
